issues.description: The specification/UML defines the saloon inventory class as "Stock" (with methods add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock) and shows SealSaloon having a Stock field. In both template and solution repositories, the corresponding implemented class is named "Inventory" and "Stock.java" is empty. This creates a naming conflict: students following the statement will implement/use Stock, but the provided API and reference solution use Inventory.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the name across all artifacts: either rename Inventory to Stock (class/file and all references, including SealSaloon) and remove the empty Stock.java, or update the problem statement/UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock and delete Stock.java to avoid a misleading duplicate.

issues.description: The problem statement requires SealSaloon to have a (static) "stock" field of type Stock. The solution implements this field as type Inventory (static final Inventory stock). Even if naming is clarified, the declared field type conflicts with the specification and can cause compilation issues for students whose SealSaloon uses Stock as required.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the SealSaloon.stock field type match the chosen inventory class name consistently (preferably change Inventory to Stock everywhere, then declare `private static final Stock stock = new Stock();`; alternatively update the specification to require `Inventory` and adjust UML/text accordingly).
